To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dopaminergic system regulates the content of the endocannabinoids, anandamide and the 2-arachidonoylglycerol, in the limbic brain regions, the nucleus accumbens and the prefrontal cortex, via activation of D2 and D1 dopamine receptors, respectively.
the dopaminergic modulation of the endocannabinoid system in the brain is mediated by both the D1 and D1 receptors and that this modulation may be important in the treatment of schizophrenia.
endogenous dopamine suppresses the endogenous cannabinoid anandamide and the endogenous cannabinergic 2-AG in a dose-dependent manner via activation of D2 and D1 receptors, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how dopamine modulates the endocannabinoid system.

the role of the endogenous cannabinoid system within the limbic system of the mammalian brain, with a particular emphasis on the role of endocannabinods as retrograde messengers within the corticostriatal and corticofrontal pathways.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of neuropsychiatric disorders such as Parkinson’s disease, schizophrenia, depression and anxiety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endocannabinoid system is a target of the dopaminergic system.
the endocannabinoid levels in the brain are regulated by the dopaminergic system, and that the dopaminergic receptors involved are of the D1 and D3 subtypes.
the effects of dopaminergic drugs upon the synthesis of endogenous cannabinoids are complex and are dependent upon the dose and the type of dopamine receptor that is activated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dopamine modulates the content of endocannabiniods in a region specific manner.

dopamine regulates the endogenous synthesis of endocannibinoids in the limbic brain, which is consistent with the idea that dopamine modulates glutamate transmission, which is a primary target for endocannabinoids.
the endocannabinoids anandamide and arachidonoglycerol (2AG) are synthesized in the brain and released from neurons to act as retrograde messengers to modulate synaptic function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the endogenous cannabinoid anandamide and the related lipid 2-arachidonoylglycerol (the major precursor to anandamide) are differentially regulated in the brain by dopaminergic transmission and that this differential regulation is dependent upon dopamine receptor activity.
endocannabinoids are regulated by dopamine in a differential manner.
the dopamine D1 receptor is a potent negative regulator of anandamide and D2 receptor agonists increase the synthesis of anandamide.
